falsification_interpretation.pre_specified_logic: If contemporaneous mapped seagrass has similar or higher 2016 overlap, 92.979% alone cannot support a special historical seagrass-to-algae conversion preference.
falsification_interpretation.test: Is historical seagrass-positive coverage of 2022 attached algae unusually high compared with 2022 mapped seagrass under the identical 2016 positive map?

report.interpretation: Descriptive geometric context only: denominator is each 2022 mapped class and background unmapped habitat is NOT observed bare ground. Comparisons may reflect the extent of historical vegetation/mapping rather than biological specialization.

reference.interpretation: Area fractions of 2016 map-positive source within each 2022 mapped class; no causal history effect, no known full sampling background or independent units.

interpretation: Among 2022 mapped attached algae, 92.979% overlaps 2016 mapped seagrass. However among contemporaneous 2022 mapped seagrass, 96.945% overlaps 2016 mapped seagrass. The historical mapped seagrass footprint is therefore not particularly enriched for attached algae relative to seagrass.
This descriptive area contrast falsifies an interpretation of the 92.979% figure alone as selective seagrass-to-algae conversion.
The result does not refute real algae turnover, does not test algae competition/causal inhibition and is not a spatially independent population inference.
The 2016-to-2022 6-year gap and 2022-to-2024 classification changes still require matched field-confirmation and exact map-footprint work.
2016 nonpositive map class is not confirmed biological absence; a future contrast must preserve it as unknown, and the 2016 mapped algae code was absent in legacy maps but not ecologically absent.
